title: Gut microbiota -derived extracellular vesicles in patients with obesity undergoing gastric bypass surgery
projectDescription: 30 obese patients undergo gastric bypass. Fecal samples were collected at baseline and 6 months after the surgery and also 9 healty subjects. EVs were isolated from feces and proteins were isolated from purified EV prep.
sampleProcessingProtocol: EVs were isolated from fecal samples by protocol earlied desceribed by Byts et al 2023. EV protein isolation was performed using methanol chloroform precipitation according to Friedman 200724. Shortly, 1 volume vesicles added with 3 volume water, 4 volume methanol and 1 volume chloroform.  Appeared precipitate was washed adding again 4 volume methanol and centrifuged precipitate to bottom of the tube. The precipitate was dried and dissolved to 1x Laemly loading buffer (Bio-Rad, USA) and water by boiling 5 min. The samples were loaded to 12% Mini-Protean TGX (Bio-Rad) gel and SDS-PAGE electrophoresis were performed at 110 V until samples were completely in the gel, roughly 10 minutes. The gel was fixed in 50% ethanol and 10 % acetic acid solution for 30 min and rinsed with water. The gel was stained by SYPRO Ruby protein gel stain (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at overnight. Excess dye was removed by washing with 5 % acetic acid for 5 min and in dd water 15 min. Gel was dried by ethanol for transport. Before mass spectrometry, samples were in-gel digested via trypsin and peptides were dissolved in 0.1 % formic acid. The LC-ESI-MS/MS analyses were performed on a nanoflow HPLC system (Easy-nLC1200, Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to the Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) equipped with a nano-electrospray ionization source. Mass spectrometry analysis was performed at the Turku Proteomics Facility, University of Turku and Åbo Akademi University.
dataProcessingProtocol: Sequences of proteomic samples were analyzed by PEAKS Studio software (version 10.6) (bioinformatics Solutions Inc., USA). For protein and peptide identification the database search was performed against Uniprot Swissprot and Uniprot trEMBL databases (v.2022_05) with parent mass error tolerance 10.0 ppm, fragment mass error tolerance 0.02 Da and FDR for both was 1.0%. Only top protein from each protein group were accepted. Proteins were identified to present if at least one unique peptide with total coverage of supporting peptide was more than 1%. Proteins presenting in negative control sample and blank were excluded from identification results.
